keyFacts: You may cross railway tracks only at a level crossing, giving way to a train ⟦1⟧

You must not enter a level crossing when the barrier is closed or beginning to close, regardless of the traffic light, or when the traffic light shows a prohibiting signal, regardless of the barrier ⟦2⟧
You must not enter a level crossing if there is a traffic jam beyond it that would force you to stop on the tracks ⟦3⟧
Slow-moving vehicles travelling at less than 8 km/h may cross a level crossing only with permission from the head of the track section ⟦4⟧
If you must not go on, stop at the stop line, sign 2.5 or the traffic light, or, if none of these are present, at the boundary of the crossing ⟦5⟧
If you get stuck on a level crossing: get everyone out of the car, clear the crossing, and if possible send two people along the tracks in both directions for 1000 m ⟦6⟧
The general alarm signal is one long and three short sound signals; the stop signal to a train is a circular movement of the arm ⟦7⟧
On a motorway, U-turns, entering service gaps in the central reservation, reversing and learner driving are prohibited ⟦8⟧
Pedestrians, bicycles, mopeds, tractors and vehicles whose speed, by specification or condition, is below 40 km/h are not allowed on a motorway ⟦9⟧
You may stop on a motorway only at areas marked with sign 5.15 or 6.11 ⟦10⟧
In a residential zone, the pedestrian has priority, and the speed is limited to 20 km/h ⟦11⟧
When leaving a residential zone, the driver gives way to everyone; the rules for a residential zone also apply in yards ⟦12⟧
mistakes: Trying to dash through while the barrier is still coming down. Entry is already prohibited once the barrier starts to close.
Entering a level crossing behind a queue of traffic. If there is a jam beyond the crossing, wait before it, or you risk being stranded on the tracks.
Driving around a queue before a level crossing using the oncoming lane. This is separately prohibited.
Reversing back to a missed exit on a motorway. Reversing and making a U-turn are prohibited there.
Sounding the horn at a pedestrian in a residential zone to make them move out of the way. There, the pedestrian has priority, and using the horn is prohibited.
Relying on the “priority to the right” rule when leaving a yard. When leaving a residential zone or a yard, you give way to everyone.
